name: Sukkah Structure and Validity
notes: Laws governing the physical construction and validity of the sukkah: height requirements, walls, schach, and related rules

name: Schach (Sukkah Roofing)
notes: Laws of valid and invalid roofing material for a sukkah, including susceptibility to impurity and attachment to the ground

name: Dofen Akumah (Curved Wall Principle)
notes: Legal principle by which part of an existing roof or ceiling is treated as an extension of the wall, enabling a sukkah to be valid

name: Yeshivat Sukkah (Dwelling in the Sukkah)
notes: Obligation to eat, sleep, and dwell in the sukkah during the seven days of the festival, including the first night obligation and exemptions

name: Exemptions from Sukkah
notes: Who is exempt from the sukkah obligation: women, minors, slaves, the ill, travelers performing a mitzvah, and rain as a sign of exemption

name: Nisuch HaMayim (Water Libation)
notes: The special water libation performed on the altar during the festival of Sukkot, including the drawing from Siloam pool and pouring procedures

name: Simchat Beit HaShoevah (Celebration of Water Drawing)
notes: The great celebration in the Temple courtyard during Sukkot associated with the water libation, including music, dancing, torches, and illumination

name: Aravah (Willow Branch Mitzva on Sukkot)
notes: The distinct mitzva of encircling the altar with willow branches on Sukkot (separate from the willow of the four species), including the seven-day and Shabbat override issues

name: Hakafot (Circling the Altar on Sukkot)
notes: The practice of circling the altar once each day of Sukkot and seven times on Hoshana Rabbah, with lulav and aravah

name: Lulav Ownership on First Day
notes: Requirement that the lulav belong to the person fulfilling the mitzva on the first day of Sukkot; inability to use a borrowed lulav on the first day

name: Waving the Lulav (Naanuim)
notes: Laws of when to wave the lulav during Hallel, in which directions, and at which verses

name: Etrog Specifications and Validity
notes: Physical requirements for a valid etrog including size, blemishes, orla status, teruma status, and color

name: Lulav, Myrtle, and Willow Specifications
notes: Physical requirements for valid lulav, hadas, and aravah, including dryness, severed tops, minimum lengths, and number of species

name: Hallel on Sukkot
notes: Recitation of the full Hallel throughout the eight days of Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret, including waving the lulav during Hallel

name: Shemini Atzeret (Eighth Day of Assembly)
notes: The eighth day following Sukkot as an independent festival, with obligations of rejoicing and Hallel but not sukkah or lulav

name: Hoshana Rabbah (Seventh Day of Sukkot)
notes: The seventh day of Sukkot on which the altar is encircled seven times and special willow-branch customs are performed

name: Priestly Watches on Festivals
notes: Distribution of festival offerings and Temple service among the 24 priestly watches during pilgrimage festivals, including equal shares and rotation of bull sacrifices on Sukkot

name: Shewbread Distribution on Festivals
notes: Rules for distribution of the shewbread among priestly watches when Shabbat coincides with or is adjacent to a festival

name: Mishmar of Bilgah (Priestly Penalty)
notes: The permanent penalty imposed on the priestly watch of Bilgah: fixed ring, sealed niche, and always dividing shewbread in the south

name: Takkanot of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai for Sukkot
hebrew: תקנות רבן יוחנן בן זכאי לסוכות
notes: Post-Temple enactments of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: lulav taken seven days everywhere, and prohibition of new grain extended through 16 Nisan as zecher lamikdash

name: Zecher laMikdash (Commemoration of Temple Practice)
notes: Rabbinic enactments instituted to remember Temple practices, such as taking lulav seven days outside the Temple after its destruction

name: Sukkot Bull Offerings (Seventy Bulls)
notes: The seventy bulls sacrificed over the seven days of Sukkot in descending order (13, 12, 11... 7), and their distribution among the priestly watches

name: Children's Obligation in Sukkah
notes: The rabbinic obligation to train children in the mitzva of sukkah once they no longer need their mother, and the incident of Shammai the Elder roofing for a newborn
